In the next year, AI will be smarter than all of us.

There'll be outliers of course… Some people will still be ahead in specific corners, because our thinking is strange in ways models can’t reproduce. We're messy compute and occasionally we'll lands somewhere a machine can't. But these are exceptions.

The Exponential Age is hitting the steep part of its curve and you can already see it.

Take Anthropic for eg. Their revenue is scaling beyond Metcalfe’s Law into Reed's Law, making it the fastest growing revenue line of any company in human history. Ludicrous when you think about it.

And it won't stop with one company. Every one of these curves feeds the next, and all of them together bend the Exponential Age into the Economic Singularity. Intelligence compounds, capital reallocates, and the system starts running at a tempo we can't even process.

We can trace all of this back to World War 2.

The reason your salary buys less, the reason your kids can't afford a house, the reason retirement keeps drifting out of reach comes back to one thing.

Demographics.

The baby boomers were the biggest generational cohort in human history, and their spending and saving habits shaped asset prices, interest rates, and policy decisions for years. Now they're retiring in numbers no economy was built to absorb.

With a shrinking workforce GDP growth stalls. Governments borrow more to fund what they owe, and print more money to foot the bill… Which means the retirement you spent decades saving for is worth less each year.

This is the crux of my Everything Code framework:  Demographics drive debt, debt drives currency debasement, and your retirement gets eaten alive.
